# Graph presets

`vault/.obsidian/graph.json` (the live graph-view state) is gitignored —
Obsidian rewrites it on every graph interaction (zoom, pan, filter tweaks),
which made it a constant source of dirty-tree pull failures across machines.
The curated views live here as full graph.json-shaped snapshots you can swap
in; `default.json` is the canonical genre-colored artist map.

## Presets

- **default** — the full artist map, MOC hubs filtered out, 13 genre color
  groups.
- **artist-web**, **rotation**, **source-follow** — the focused variants
  (see each file's `search` query).

## Switching

With Obsidian running (preferred — live switch, no file races):

```sh
vault/.obsidian/graph-presets/apply.sh rotation
```

The script targets the `Music` vault — Chris's local Obsidian working copy
regenerated by `obsidian_driver.py --out Music` — since that's the copy
actually opened in Obsidian; edit `vault=` in the script if your working
vault is named differently.

With Obsidian **closed**, a plain file copy works too
(`cp <preset>.json ../graph.json`). Never copy over `graph.json` while
Obsidian is open — the app holds graph state in memory and writes it back
over your edit, which is why file-based switching gave inconsistent results.

## Saving a new preset

Get the graph looking right in Obsidian, then snapshot the live state from
the open vault's `.obsidian/graph.json` into a new file here.
